examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A decider halts on every input with the correct membership answer; a recognizer must accept members but may loop on nonmembers. A Turing machine's unbounded tape is a model, not a fixed finite storage bound. Decidable languages are recognizable, and a language is decidable when both it and its complement are recognizable. Dovetailing simulates two possibly nonhalting recognizers fairly until one accepts.

**Key relationship:** Decidable = machine halts with an answer on every input

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Separate halting guarantees from acceptance correctness.
2. Check member and nonmember cases.
3. Use dovetailing when both sides are recognizable.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A recognizer must accept every member but may loop on a nonmember. A decider must halt on every input and accept exactly the members. For recognizable-language intersection, dovetail recognizers so one nonterminating run cannot prevent progress of another. A bounded simulation is finite and can be used in reductions or enumerations.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A machine accepts 3 of 8 given inputs, rejects 4, and loops on 1. How many inputs does it halt on?

**Answer: 7.** Acceptance and rejection are both halting outcomes, so it halts on 3+4=7 inputs. Because one input loops, this behaviour cannot be a decider on a domain containing all eight inputs.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A machine halting on every input need not decide a particular named language unless its acceptance and rejection sets also match that language.

Not accepting is not the same as rejecting when nontermination is possible.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A decider must:

- **A.** Have finitely bounded tape
- **B.** Halt only on members
- **C.** Halt on every input with correct acceptance/rejection
- **D.** Accept every input

**Answer: C.** Total halting plus correct answers distinguishes a decider from a general recognizer.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Every decidable language is recognizable
- **B.** Recognizable always means decidable
- **C.** Recognizable L and recognizable complement imply decidable L
- **D.** Recognizers may loop on nonmembers

**Answer: A, C, D.** Dovetail the two recognizers; exactly one must eventually accept. A recognizer alone lacks this total-halting guarantee.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Two recognizers are dovetailed one step each per round. The accepting recognizer needs 7 steps. Maximum rounds to see its acceptance?



**Answer: 7.** Fair scheduling gives each machine one step per round; after seven rounds the accepting one has executed its seven steps.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q13 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/turing-machines?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Turing machines and recognizable languages. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A decider must halt with acceptance on every member of L and halt with rejection on every nonmember. Both correctness directions and termination are required.
2. Merely halting (A) could decide a different language. Accepting all members alone (B) or rejecting all nonmembers alone (C) leaves the other cases unspecified.
3. Only the combined statement **D** is equivalent to deciding L.
